newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister says costs to telecom rivals cut.
newsitem.headline: French minister says costs to telecom rivals cut.

text.p: Francois Fillon, French minister of post and telecommunications, told the Le Monde newspaper on Wednesday the costs to future France Telecom rivals had been cut without hurting the currently state-owned group.

He said that the costs of the so-called universal service of telecommunications -- basic services, connections in remote areas and emergency services -- would be some six billion francs per year, instead of the nine billion France Telecom had proposed.
The final cost has to be established by the regulator, Autorite de Reglementation de Telecommunications (ART).
France Telecom is responsible for providing the universal service but other operators have to chip in to share the costs.

"The figure will be proposed to the ART before September 1. It will be significantly less than the nine billion (francs) mentioned in 1996, without doubt close to six billion francs," Fillon said in an interview.
He also said that ART would decide before the end of the month on the interconnection charges that France Telecom can ask from rival operators for the use of its lines or switches.
Fillon said that a new price list was lower than one previously proposed by France Telecom.
"We have found a balance. We will have tariffs that are comparable, all things being equal, to what is available in other countries, allowing competition to take place," he said.
"They also take account of the use of France Telecom's network and allow it to continue its development," he added.
He said new telecoms operators would be obliged to devote a part of their resources to research in the telecoms sector.
"For France Telecom it will be four percent of sales, which is five billion francs," he said.
"For the new operators, it will be five percent of their investments. That will be included in their licences," Fillon said.
The French telecommunications market will be open to full competition in 1998 and Fillon said that the first licences for operators competing with France Telecom could be delivered before the summer.
Declared rivals so far are the Cegetel unit of Cie Generale des Eaux, which is teamed up with British Telecom Plc and Mannesmann, which will compete with a joint venture between Bouygues and STET.

The French government plans to partially privatise France Telecom in the coming months, aiming to raise at least 25 billion francs. Fillon did not elaborate on the share sale in the Le Monde newspaper.
